endorsements.quote: Use an institutional attestation policy requiring explicit review of AI drafts, an audit trail of edits, faculty cosignature for any trainee-associated AI-drafted content, and education on accountability and liability.

Require learners to generate the assessment and plan before viewing any AI draft; mandate periodic AI-free encounters, with frequency determined by training seniority level; explicitly assess reasoning, not just final notes.

Build equity monitoring into deployment from day 1; teach learners to detect and escalate differential performance; require vendor disclosure of training data and performance disaggregated by patient demographics.
Teach explicit, repeatable patient consent scripts as a clinical skill.
Define and assess AI literacy competencies at the UME and GME level, including mechanics, failure modes, equity, consent, and attestation, before deploying ambient tools.
Faculty will need training on how to effectively teach and supervise students when using ambient AI and when best to introduce these tools.

unlisted_practices: Require medical students to write unaided clinical notes by default and permit AI-drafted notes only after demonstrated competence and only as a comparison exercise.

Conduct rigorous research, such as multicenter randomized crossover, stepped-wedge, or parallel-group trials, on the impact of ambient AI on trainee learning outcomes, note quality, clinical reasoning, and cognitive load.
Obtain written learner consent for any educational recording with defined retention and use limits and separate formative from summative use.
Keep AI-generated feedback on trainee encounters formative and separate from grading, use validated rubrics, and pilot-evaluate feedback quality before learner rollout.
Use structured side-by-side comparison of AI and trainee notes in early PGY-1 and conduct periodic competency checks.
Tailor trainee ambient AI education to each specialty rather than using a one-size-fits-all training plan.

screen.reason: This is a viewpoint article discussing the opportunities, challenges, and necessary guardrails of integrating ambient AI scribes into medical education.
